title: docs(qa): re-point identity-auth.api-key-ui-lifecycle's revoke oracle to 403 API_KEY_REVOKED
body:
Fixes #23992
Clause-②: no

The platform-checklist item `identity-auth.api-key-ui-lifecycle` expected a revoked API key's next `x-api-key` call to answer `401`. Since the API-key lifecycle (#23367 ruling A, executed by #23541), a recognised but revoked key is refused `403` with `error.code` `API_KEY_REVOKED`. Only an unknown key still gets the generic `401`. So the item scored a correct runtime red. This PR re-points step 4 and acceptance clause 2 to the shape that shipped, bumps `revision` 1 → 2, and appends a `history` row naming #23992, #23367 and #23541. The diff is `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` only (+10 / −8, one entry). There is no product code change.

The clause is not loosened. A revoked key that answers `200` or serves any row still fails it. So does a post-revoke refusal that is the generic `401`, or a `403` carrying any other code. Step 5 (restore → `200`) is unchanged. The oracle scores the status, the code and the absence of rows. It pins none of the refusal message's wording, because the lifecycle owner rewords that text (#23944, PR #23991). This matches what PR #24000 did for the MCP revocation clauses.

## Old and new text

**Step 4** (`steps[4]`)

- Old: `revoke the key via the row action revoke_api_key (PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_api_key/{id} bodyExtra {revoked:true}); immediately re-call the data route with x-api-key and capture the 401`
- New: `revoke the key via the row action revoke_api_key (PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_api_key/{id} bodyExtra {revoked:true}); immediately re-call the data route with x-api-key and capture the 403 whose body's error.code is API_KEY_REVOKED and which carries no rows (a recognised key its own lifecycle refuses — only an UNKNOWN key gets the generic 401)`

**Acceptance clause 2** (`acceptance[2]`)

- Old clause: `revoke is immediate and enforced server-side: after revoke_api_key the same x-api-key call 401s on the very next request`
- Old verify: `the post-revoke x-api-key request returns 401`
- Old evidence: `the revoke PATCH response + the 401`
- New clause: `revoke is immediate and enforced server-side: after revoke_api_key the same x-api-key call is refused on the very next request with the key's own lifecycle refusal — 403, error.code API_KEY_REVOKED, and no rows. Since #23367 (executed by #23541) a recognised but revoked key is refused 403 API_KEY_REVOKED; the generic 401 answers only a key the server does not recognise at all. The refusal's message is the key's own lifecycle message and its wording is NOT pinned here: the code is what a client branches on, and the lifecycle owner rewords that text (#23944)`
- New verify: `the post-revoke x-api-key request returns HTTP 403 and its body's error.code is API_KEY_REVOKED, with no record rows in the body (packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts#lifecycleRefusalOf decides it; the data routes answer it through packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts#enforceAuth). Score the status, the code and the absence of rows, never the message's wording. A 200 or any served row, a generic 401, or a 403 carrying any other code is a FAIL — the last means the key was accepted and something later refused`
- New evidence: `the revoke PATCH response + the 403 API_KEY_REVOKED refusal body`

**Also in the same entry**

- `negative[1]` keeps its text and adds the other failure direction: a post-revoke refusal that is the generic `401`, or carries any code other than `API_KEY_REVOKED`, is a FAIL.
- `source` gains one row: `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts#lifecycleRefusalOf` + `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts#enforceAuth`. Both anchors resolve under `check-platform-checklist`.
- `history` gains the `revision: 2` row (`ref: #23992`).

## The source lines (at `origin/main` `e18b23fac`)

- `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts:217`: `const API_KEY_REVOKED_REFUSAL = { code: 'API_KEY_REVOKED', status: 403 } as const;`
- `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts:299` starts `lifecycleRefusalOf`. Its first arm (lines 306-321), `if (row.revoked === true || row.revoked === 1)`, returns `code: API_KEY_REVOKED_REFUSAL.code` (line 308) with the located message. `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:501` raises it as the branded `ApiKeyLifecycleRefusalError`, whose status is `API_KEY_LIFECYCLE_REFUSAL_STATUS` = 403 (`api-key.ts:228`).
- `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:3493-3495`: the context resolver remembers the branded refusal beside the request. Lines 2478-2481: `enforceAuth` answers `res.status(lifecycle.status).json({ error: { code: lifecycle.code, message: lifecycle.message } })`. A request with no remembered refusal falls through to the generic anonymous `401`.
- Permanent pin of that relay: `packages/rest/src/rest-api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts`, "revoked, expired and inactive answer 403 with three distinct codes".

## Re-run record: #24011

`QA run · identity-auth.api-key-ui-lifecycle (1/1) · e1e711ae · 2026-10-16 · 1 PASS / 0 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED / 0 NOT-RUN`. `node scripts/qa/qa-rollup.mjs` parses the title (row `#24011`, `1/1`, sha `e1e711ae`).

The run used a real showcase boot built from this branch's tree (`e1e711ae2`; product tree `origin/main` `e18b23fac`). `pnpm build` ran 75/75 tasks. The console was built at the `.objectui-sha` pin `f8267df93aba` with `pnpm objectui:build`, and `check:console-sha` was green. The server ran on its own port (41873) and its own file DB, and was stopped by PID afterwards. Personas were the seeded admin and members minted by invite + sign-up. The browser legs were driven through Playwright (Chromium 141).

| # | clause | verdict | evidence (short) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | secret shown once | pass | mint 201 with a raw `key`; get-by-id (owner and admin) and the mine list carry no `key` field, only `prefix`; the dialog showed the raw value, and after Done it is gone from the page |
| 1 | key = owner's view | pass | `showcase_task` via `x-api-key` 200, 10 rows, the same id set as the owner's session. On `showcase_inquiry` the admin sees 3 rows, the owner's session 0 and the owner's key 0 |
| 2 | revoke → 403 `API_KEY_REVOKED` | pass | PATCH `{"revoked": true}` 200. The very next read answered 403 with body `{"error": {"code": "API_KEY_REVOKED", "message": …}}` and no rows, and a repeat answered the same. Through the console's Revoke API Key row action, the request body was `{"revoked":true}` and the next two reads answered 403 `API_KEY_REVOKED`. Control: an unknown key answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` |
| 3 | restore → 200 | pass | PATCH `{"revoked": false}` 200, then a read answered 200 with 10 rows. The console's Restore API Key row action gave the same result |
| 4 | mine-view scoping | pass | The second member's mine list and unfiltered list both exclude the owner's key, and get-by-id answers 404. With two owners, each one's mine list shows only its own key. The admin's all_keys list (API and Setup → API Keys) shows every owner's key |
| 5 | dialog + list screenshots | pass | The dialog shows "not be shown again", the secret and Copy. The re-opened My Keys list shows name + prefix rows only |

## Acceptance notes

- PR #23991 (#23944) landed before this branch was cut. The card suggested also checking that the message names "Restore API Key". This PR does not do that, because the dispatch ruling says the oracle never scores the prose. The live message does name the Restore API Key action, but that was observed, not scored.
- Two dogfood files, `api-key-revoke-lifecycle` and `api-key-owner-revoke`, accept a generic `401` as well as `403 API_KEY_REVOKED` for a revoked key. The strict `403` + code relay is pinned only at unit level (`packages/rest/src/rest-api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts`), and this item has no `automated.ref`. Carrier: none.
- The item's `source` row for `sys-api-key.object.ts` still says `apiMethods ['get','list']`, but the object declares `['get', 'list', 'update']`. This is a stale annotation that scores nothing, so it is outside this card's class and was left untouched. Carrier: none.
- Scope: `negative[1]` and `source[]` are inside the claimed entry but outside the claim's parenthetical field list. Both carry the ruling's "do not loosen" rule and the citation it asks for.
